claims.nodeLabel: 50 U.S.C. 3091a - Congressional Oversight of Controlled Access Programs
claims.sourceText: Full text of 50 U.S.C. 3091a, by omission
claims.text: Section 3091a contains no waiver authority of any kind.

claims.nodeLabel: 50 U.S.C. 3091a - Congressional Oversight of Controlled Access Programs
claims.text: (d)(3) verbatim: "The term 'controlled access program' means a program created or managed pursuant to Intelligence Community Directive 906, or successor directive." The GPO 'References in Text' note states: 'Intelligence Community Directive 906, referred to in subsec. (d)(3), is located at https://www.dni.gov/files/documents/ICD/ICD906.pdf.' Congress incorporated an executive-branch directive by reference and pointed at a URL, so the statutory scope of 'controlled access program' moves whenever ODNI reissues ICD 906.

claims.nodeLabel: 50 U.S.C. 3091a - Congressional Oversight of Controlled Access Programs
claims.text: 50 U.S.C. 3091a(b)(2)(B) permits transfer without prior notification where the head determines it 'is required to mitigate an urgent counterintelligence issue' or 'is necessary to maintain access in the event of an organizational restructuring.'

claims.nodeLabel: 50 U.S.C. 3091a - Congressional Oversight of Controlled Access Programs
claims.text: 50 U.S.C. 3091a(d)(2) requires each annual report to list all active compartments and subcompartments, all terminated during the period, and for the DNI a certification that creation, validation or substantial modification of every program is 'substantiated and justified', with 'the identification of a control officer for each controlled access program' and 'a statement of protection requirements'.

claims.nodeLabel: 50 U.S.C. 3091a - Congressional Oversight of Controlled Access Programs
claims.text: NO WAIVER. 50 U.S.C. 3091a contains no subsection permitting the DNI or an IC element head to waive, defer, or narrow the briefing, notification, or reporting duties, and no reduction of the audience to chairs and ranking members. This is the structural opposite of 10 U.S.C. 119(e).

claims.nodeLabel: 50 U.S.C. 3091a - Congressional Oversight of Controlled Access Programs
claims.text: 50 U.S.C. 3091a(c), added by Pub. L. 118-159 sec. 6602: NIP funds 'may not be obligated or expended for any controlled access program, or a compartment or subcompartment therein, until the head of the element ... submits the notification required by subsection (b).'

claims.nodeLabel: 50 U.S.C. 3091a - Congressional Oversight of Controlled Access Programs
claims.text: (b) verbatim: 'A head of an element of the intelligence community may not establish a controlled access program, or a compartment or subcompartment therein, until the head notifies the appropriate congressional committees and congressional leadership of such controlled access program, compartment, or subcompartment, as the case may be.' The notification duty reaches down to the sub-compartment level.

claims.text: 50 U.S.C. 3091a(e)(3): 'The term "controlled access program" means a program created or managed pursuant to Intelligence Community Directive 906, or successor directive.'

claims.nodeLabel: 50 U.S.C. 3091a - Congressional Oversight of Controlled Access Programs
claims.text: (c)(2)(A)-(B): each annual report must include 'A list of all compartments and subcompartments of controlled access programs active as of the date of the report' and 'A list of all compartments and subcompartments of controlled access programs terminated during the period covered by the report.' (c)(2)(C) requires the DNI additionally to certify that the creation, validation or substantial modification of every existing and proposed CAP 'are substantiated and justified', with the rationale, an identified control officer, and a statement of protection requirements for each.

claims.text: The section requires an annual report containing 'a list of all compartments and subcompartments of controlled access programs active as of the date of the report' and 'a list of all compartments and subcompartments of controlled access programs terminated during the period'. A complete compartment inventory is therefore owed to Congress by statute, whatever is or is not delivered.

claims.nodeLabel: 50 U.S.C. 3091a - Congressional Oversight of Controlled Access Programs
claims.text: 50 U.S.C. 3091a(b)(2)(A), added by Pub. L. 118-159 sec. 6603 (23 December 2024): a head of an IC element 'may not transfer a capability from a controlled access program, including from a compartment or subcompartment therein to a compartment or subcompartment of another controlled access program, to a special access program (as defined in section 3348(g) of this title), or to anything else outside the controlled access program, until the head submits to the appropriate congressional committees and congressional leadership notice of the intent of the head to make such transfer.'

claims.nodeLabel: 50 U.S.C. 3091a - Congressional Oversight of Controlled Access Programs
claims.text: (a)(1) verbatim: 'Not less frequently than semiannually or upon request by one of the appropriate congressional committees or a member of congressional leadership, the Director of National Intelligence shall provide to such committees and congressional leadership a briefing on each controlled access program in effect.' There is no exception for unacknowledged CAPs.

claims.nodeLabel: 50 U.S.C. 3091a - Congressional Oversight of Controlled Access Programs
claims.text: Source credit, verbatim: '(July 26, 1947, ch. 343, title V, Sec. 501A, as added Pub. L. 117-103, div. X, title V, Sec. 504, Mar. 15, 2022, 136 Stat. 986.)' -- i.e. enacted in the Intelligence Authorization Act for FY2022 carried in the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2022.

claims.nodeLabel: 50 U.S.C. 3091a - Congressional Oversight of Controlled Access Programs
claims.text: (d)(1)-(2) define 'appropriate congressional committees' as the congressional intelligence committees plus both Appropriations Committees, and 'congressional leadership' as the Senate majority and minority leaders and the Speaker and minority leader of the House -- i.e. a statutory Gang-of-Eight-shaped audience that is a floor, not a ceiling.

claims.locator: b)(2) as added by Pub. L. 118-159 sec. 6603
claims.nodeLabel: 50 U.S.C. 3091a - Congressional Oversight of Controlled Access Programs
claims.sourceText: 50 U.S.C. 3091a(b)(2) as added by Pub. L. 118-159 sec. 6603
claims.text: Section 6603 of the FY2025 NDAA is a statutory response to the possibility that a capability is moved between compartment regimes to escape the notification that attaches to each. The exception for 'organizational restructuring' is the gap it leaves: a reorganisation is a self-certified determination by the same official making the transfer. Reasoning: reading the prohibition together with its own exception.

claims.nodeLabel: 50 U.S.C. 3091a - Congressional Oversight of Controlled Access Programs
claims.text: Because 3091a(d)(3) defines its own subject matter by reference to ICD 906, and ICD 906 section C.3 expressly excludes DoD, State, Energy, DHS, DOJ and NSC covert-action programs, the strongest CAP oversight statute on the books cannot reach a program held on the DoD side of the line. Moving a program from IC cognizance to DoD cognizance moves it from a no-waiver statute to a waiver statute. Reasoning stated from 3091a(d)(3) and ICD 906 C.3.

claims.nodeLabel: The four SAP reporting regimes and the seams between them
claims.text: Only 50 U.S.C. 3091a carries a funding prohibition tied to notification, added by section 6602 of Public Law 118-159 on 23 December 2024.

claims.nodeLabel: The four SAP reporting regimes and the seams between them
claims.sourceText: Comparison of 10 U.S.C. 119(e), 50 U.S.C. 2426(e), 50 U.S.C. 3348(e) and 50 U.S.C. 3091a
claims.text: Of the four regimes, only 10 U.S.C. 119(e)(2) and 50 U.S.C. 2426(e)(2) narrow the recipient of waived information to the chairman and ranking minority member; 50 U.S.C. 3348(e)(2) keeps the full oversight committees, and 50 U.S.C. 3091a has no waiver provision at all.

claims.nodeLabel: The four SAP reporting regimes and the seams between them
claims.text: A program moved between the DoD and IC regimes changes both its governing statute and its reporting audience, and before 23 December 2024 no statute required notice of the move. That is a documented, lawful, unnotified route by which a program's oversight history can be broken. Reasoning: the prohibition added by Pub. L. 118-159 sec. 6603 did not exist before that date and operates prospectively.

claims.nodeLabel: The Gang of Eight and the limited-notification convention
claims.text: By contrast 50 U.S.C. 3091a(d)(2) writes an eight-person leadership set INTO the mandatory audience for every controlled access program: 'the majority leader of the Senate; the minority leader of the Senate; the Speaker of the House of Representatives; and the minority leader of the House of Representatives,' alongside the intelligence and appropriations committees. Here the eight is a floor added to committee notice, not a substitute for it.

edges.note: Pub. L. 118-159 secs. 6602 and 6603, approved 23 December 2024, amend this section: 6602 inserts a new subsection (c) limiting National Intelligence Program spending, and 6603 adds subsection (b)(2)(A) with its exception at (B). The OLRC text carries the amendment note and records that subsection (c) 'shall apply with respect to controlled access programs ... that are established on or after the date of the enactment of this Act', so the new limit is prospective only and existing compartments are untouched by it. Statute read on 22 August 2026; the verbatim section text is already on the amendment node from the enacted public law.
